subject.title: Plugin install doesn't build native bindings — plugins with better-sqlite3 fail on Node 24 (ABI v137) with bindings file not found

question: Should OpenClaw keep npm plugin installs script-disabled and add native-addon diagnostics, or add a trusted/manifest-gated native rebuild path for plugins that need compiled bindings?
rationale: The observable bug is real, but the most direct fix runs lifecycle/build scripts from third-party plugin dependency trees, which changes a deliberate safe-install boundary.

options.title: Keep Safe Default And Add Diagnostics
options.body: Preserve --ignore-scripts by default and add detection plus actionable install/doctor/runtime errors for missing native bindings, with a later explicit trust-gated rebuild design if needed.

options.title: Add Manifest-Gated Rebuild Support
options.body: Allow plugin publishers or trusted installs to request targeted rebuilds after security review, then require tests and live proof for both allowed and denied paths.

options.title: Run Rebuilds Automatically
options.body: Make plugin install run npm rebuild for native packages, accepting broader third-party code execution during install for better compatibility.

recommendation.title: Keep Safe Default And Add Diagnostics
recommendation.body: Preserve --ignore-scripts by default and add detection plus actionable install/doctor/runtime errors for missing native bindings, with a later explicit trust-gated rebuild design if needed.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current per-plugin managed npm project topology and are the strongest history signal for deciding install-flow security and compatibility tradeoffs.
